_: Indexing benchmark: bethanechol chloride. Transcribed from the PUBLISHED TABLES of Bergmann et al. (2004); no program output is used. See tests/data/README.md.

source.citation: Bergmann, J., Le Bail, A., Shirley, R. & Zlokazov, V. (2004). Renewed interest in powder diffraction data indexing. Z. Kristallogr. 219, 783-790.
source.tables: Table 6 (the ten 20-line position sets) and Table 5 (the per-program scores).
source.transcription: Positions typed from the printed Table 6, which is laid out row-major with ten columns; they are reproduced here column-wise as ten named sets. Intensities are NOT in the paper's table (it points at the UPPW web site for them) and are not carried: every set is positions only, which is exactly what PeakList.from_positions is for.
source.verified_by: Three checks in tests/test_acceptance_indexing.py, each against a statement the paper makes but does not tabulate. (1) C = A - 0.100 and D = B - 0.100 on all 80 values, the zeroshift correction the text describes. (2) Every B line inside A's 2theta range is bit-identical to an A line, B being the I>=5% subset of the same measurement. (3) The published cell leaves exactly 3 of the 20 lines unexplained in every 46-1964 set, against the text's '3 impurity lines among the first 35', and 7 of the first 20 in 43-1748, against '8 impurity lines among the first 26'.

answer._: The paper's Table-5 caption and closing paragraph. The cell is the one refined against set F, which is why F's deviations are ~0 by construction and the other nine sets are an independent test of it.
answer.structure_solved_in: Le Bail, A. & Stephens, P. W., cited as 'to be published' in reference [20]; the paper states this is the one UPPW case where the cell was confirmed by a complete structure determination.

scoring._: The paper's own rule, from the text preceding Table 5.
scoring.range: +/-20 (ten sets x two modes: default and manual)

first_4.what: Best of ITO13, DICVOL91, TREOR90 and McMaille run outside Crysfire — the bar this package is graded against.

best_of_all.what: Best result from every program in Table 5, including the Crysfire suite.

individual_globals._: Table 5's Global column, for the programs run outside Crysfire.

manual_mode._: The paper's own manual-mode conditions, quoted from the 'Special conditions' section, adopted wholesale rather than invented (CLAUDE.md: adopt the protocol, do not borrow the numbers). Every classic program was allowed these.
manual_mode.quoted_from: McMaille manual mode: '8 unindexed lines are tolerated, successive runs are made, the solution being found in a monoclinic run with volume range 800-1200 A^3, and 5-20 A cell parameters.'

default_mode._: The paper's stated default bar: 'The programs' default values should preferably be applied in all crystal symmetries, or at least with maximum cell parameters of 20 A and Vmax = 2000 A^3 in monoclinic symmetry.'

Da.treatment: zeroshift corrected and I >= 5% (B minus 0.100 deg)

Db.treatment: zeroshift corrected and I >= 5% (B minus 0.100 deg)

impurity_statement._: The paper's own count, in the text: the benchmark's difficulty is these lines, not the zeroshift.
impurity_statement.43-1748: 8 impurity lines among the first 26 lines
impurity_statement.46-1964: 3 impurity lines among the first 35 lines

zeroshift_statement._: The paper's own words. Its cause is a HYPOTHESIS the paper could not test — see tests/test_acceptance_indexing.py, which tests it.
zeroshift_statement.text: both patterns have a surprisingly large zeropoint error that is close to 0.10 (2theta) deg
zeroshift_statement.hypothesis: The fact that the two ICDD Grant-in-Aid entries of the same compound, bethanechol chloride, came to present similar large zeroshifts would be consistent with a systematic specimen-displacement error of this kind.
